name: Memory Misattribution
description: People can remember content yet misremember where it came from — whether it was perceived, imagined, suggested by someone else, or encountered in another context. The memory feels real, but its source tag is wrong.
design_relevance_note: Most relevant to research interpretation rather than interface mechanics: users, teammates, or stakeholders can remember a claim, preference, or incident correctly enough to sound confident while misremembering whether it came from actual use, speculation, another person, or a prior version.
prevalence_note: A core academic memory construct, but rarely named explicitly in day-to-day product-design discussion outside careful user-research or legal/trust contexts.

findings.description: The source-monitoring literature shows that people can misattribute the origin of remembered mental experiences, confusing whether information came from perception, imagination, another person, or another context; such source errors are a central route into memory distortions and some false memories.
